Choice: Option 2: CTX936TR-ND surface mount oscillator

This is particularly important because we are not sure of the electrical characteristics of the PCB, which could affect the oscillation of a crystal. docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This page presents the final schematic of my individual subsystem, the Spray Actuator, for the OpenField project (Team 101, designer Thanh Huynh — TTH). The subsystem receives spray commands from the team's Master board over UART and drives a 12 V solenoid valve through a logic-level MOSFET. It is powered from a 9–12 V DC input that also supplies a local 5 V rail for the microcontroller.

Download Final Schematic PDF

Figure 1: Final schematic — OpenField Spray Actuator subsystem, Team 101 (click to enlarge, or download the PDF for full resolution).

docs.title: Design Summary
docs.text: Function Implementation Controller Microchip PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano (U1), mounted on two 1×28 sockets. The external 5 V rail feeds the Nano's VTG pin, and VOFF is tied to GND. Power input 9–12 V DC barrel jack (J1), with test point TP1 on the input rail (VIN). Fuse Removable 1 A time-lag 5×20 mm fuse (F1) in two Keystone 3517 clips, between the jack and the VIN rail. 5 V regulator LM7805 (U2, TO-220) with 0.33 µF input and 0.1 µF / 10 µF output capacitors, a 100 µF bulk capacitor on VIN, and 0.1 µF decoupling at the Nano. Test point TP2 on +5V. Solenoid driver IRLZ44N logic-level N-MOSFET (Q1) as a low-side switch. Gate driven from RB3 through the SPRAY_EN jumper (JP1) and a 220 Ω gate resistor, with a 100 kΩ gate pull-down so the solenoid stays off at reset. Flyback protection 1N5819 Schottky diode (D1) across the solenoid (cathode to VIN, anode to the MOSFET drain). Actuator 12 V solenoid valve connected at the 2-pin screw terminal J5 (+ = VIN, − = MOSFET drain). A red "SPRAY ON" LED (D2, 2.2 kΩ) lights while the solenoid is energized. UART to Master Nano UART on RC2 (TX) / RC3 (RX) with 1 kΩ series resistors, through the 2×4 team ribbon header J2. R3 is an optional, unpopulated (DNP) level-shift resistor position. Debug LED Green debug LED (D3) on RD6 through a 470 Ω resistor. Pushbutton Hardware-debounced pushbutton (SW1) on RD5: 10 kΩ pull-up, 1 kΩ series resistor and 1 µF capacitor (RC debounce). Test points TP1 VIN, TP2 +5V, TP3/TP8 GND, TP4 SPRAY_EN, TP5 solenoid drain, TP6 SPRAY_RX, TP7 SPRAY_TX. Expansion header J4 (1×6): +5V, RA0, RA1, RA2, RA5, GND.

docs.title: Final Specifications
docs.text: Item Value Project OpenField Team 101 Designer Thanh Huynh (TTH) Subsystem Spray Actuator Board size 97 × 78 mm Layers 2 Controller PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano Actuator 12 V solenoid Communication UART

docs.title: PCB Design Summary
docs.text:
• Functional placement. The board is arranged by function: power input along the top-left edge, the solenoid driver in the top-right corner, the regulator, LEDs, button and expansion header in the middle, the Curiosity Nano across the lower half, and the team UART header J2 in the bottom-right corner. Four M3 mounting holes sit near the corners.
  • 9–12 V to 5 V power section. Barrel jack J1 → removable fuse F1 → VIN rail → LM7805 (U2) → +5 V rail for the Nano and logic. Input, output and bulk capacitors sit next to the regulator.
  • Solenoid / MOSFET high-current routing. The main VIN and solenoid-current paths (J1 → F1 → J5 → Q1) use 1.5 mm traces; short low-current branches (≤ 50 mA) and +5 V / GND use 1.0 mm. The flyback diode D1 sits directly beside terminal J5 and MOSFET Q1 to keep the switching loop small.
  • Ground planes on both layers. Both copper layers are filled with GND and joined by stitching vias, giving every signal a continuous return path.
  • UART interface. SPRAY_TX and SPRAY_RX run from the Nano (RC2/RC3) through 1 kΩ series resistors to J2 pins 5 and 7, with pin 8 as GND. They are routed at least 30 mm away from the high-current solenoid traces.
  • USB accessibility. The Nano's USB connector faces the left board edge (marked "USB"), so it can be programmed and debugged while mounted.
  • Test points / debugging. Eight labelled test points (VIN, +5V, two GND, SPRAY_EN, solenoid drain, SPRAY_RX, SPRAY_TX), a green debug LED, a red "SPRAY ON" LED, a debounced pushbutton, a SPRAY_EN jumper (JP1) and a 6-pin expansion header (J4).
  • Silkscreen. Designer and team identification (TTH, TEAM 101, SPRAY SUBSYSTEM), connector labels, pin-1 markers and polarity marks (+/−, K, triangles). All silkscreen lines are at least 0.15 mm wide and at least 0.2 mm from any pad.

Figure 2: Final PCB, 3D angled view.

Figure 3: Top layout (left) and bottom layout, mirrored (right), rendered from the final manufacturing Gerbers: copper, solder-mask openings, silkscreen and drills.
